labels: all (study-wide CT and criteria rows, both groups)
cohorts.subjects: Living patients with symptomatic degenerative lumbar spinal stenosis (DLSS), enrolled 2008 to 2012 following the authors' earlier project (Abbas et al. 2020 [16]); each had stenosis at one or more levels, a dural sac cross-section area under 100 mm2 (after Schonstrom [8]), from degeneration of the segment; diagnosis from clinical symptoms and signs with CT; clinical inclusion criteria after SPORT [17, 18], applied by a spine surgeon co-author (KH). Israel; the ethics committee of Carmel Medical Center, Haifa approved the study; where these patients were scanned is not stated. Ethnicity not stated. Excluded: age under 40 years; congenital stenosis (bony canal AP under 12 mm, after Verbiest [19]); fractures; spondylolysis; tumors; Paget's disease; steroid treatment; severe lumbar scoliosis over 20 deg; iatrogenic conditions. The level of each patient's stenosis is not given. Mean age 66.2 +/- 11 (men) and 62 +/- 8 (women); BMI 28.9 +/- 4 and 31.4 +/- 5 (Table 1).
cohorts.n_units: L1 to L5 of 165 patients (Inference: up to 825 vertebrae; per-level n not printed)

labels: all (study-wide CT and criteria rows, both groups)
cohorts.subjects: Living patients without spinal stenosis symptoms referred to the Department of Radiology, Carmel Medical Center, Haifa, Israel, for abdominal CT for renal colic symptoms or abdominal pain; the abstract calls them individuals from the general population. Ethnicity not stated. The exclusions are printed after the stenosis group's description as exclusions from the study; Inference: the controls' minimum age of 40 and Table 3's lowest control band (12.1-14 mm) suggest the age and canal exclusions applied to them too. Mean age 62.8 +/- 12 (men) and 62 +/- 12 (women); BMI 27.3 +/- 4 and 27.6 +/- 5 (Table 1).
cohorts.n_units: L1 to L5 of 180 patients (Inference: up to 900 vertebrae; per-level n not printed)

techniques.how: Vertebral body length (VL): longest line joining the anterior and posterior body borders; width (VW): longest line joining the right and left body borders; both on the axial slice at mid vertebral height, L1 to L5. Method after Berry et al. 1987 [20] (printed Perry), adapted to CT.

techniques.observers: Intratester: one author (JA) measured twice 3-5 days apart; intertester: JA and KH within an hour; both blinded; 20 individuals; ICC 0.782 to 0.985 intra and 0.721 to 0.980 inter, all measures pooled. Who measured the full sample is not stated (Inference: JA)

L1 to L5. Table 3 bins the same AP values into bands.

within_paper: The DLSS (165) and control (180) groups are different people (p. 2, PDF 2). Every table measure (VL, VW, AP, ML, CSA, ILA, LI, beveling) was taken on the same CT scans of the same 345 patients, so Tables 1 to 5 and Figures 5 and 6 share subjects; Table 3 bins the AP diameters of Table 2's subjects with the sexes pooled, and Table 5's regression uses the same patients (pp. 2 to 6). The 20 individuals of the reliability study are of unstated group (p. 2); Inference: drawn from the 345. The abstract's numbers restate Tables 1, 2 and 5 (p. 1).
